Regenerated 2026-09-18 by the recorded recipe, which closes the last of the lib 180ba308 absolute-path residue: provenance.gen.go and provenance.json held paths from the machine that wrote them and now hold the redacted portable form. No binding output changed; the full run reproduces all of them byte for byte from the unpinned header.

The same run deleted nvidia/nvml/constants.provenance.json, and the supplemental -constants-only run that was its only producer has been removed from this record. That receipt exists to say constants.gen.go came from a different header than the rest of the package, which is the state -constants-only creates and a full run ends; cmd/nvml-survey removes it for exactly that reason (clearConstantsReceipt). The divergence it described was already gone -- the full unpinned run reproduces constants.gen.go byte for byte -- so the file survived only because the run that should have swept it wrote to a scratch directory and was hand-applied. It also could not be reproduced anywhere: its inputs entry is an absolute path inside $TMPDIR/work/nvml, a tree that no longer exists, and internal/nvidiaprovenance digests the path along with the bytes, so its source_hash is a digest over that spelling and no other machine can recompute it.

The deleted receipt remains citable by content: git blob c00343a6c623768daa24228c0b93998a83930ba4, introduced by commit 391c6f4b "nvidia/nvml: add public macro constants", retrievable with git show 391c6f4b:nvidia/nvml/constants.provenance.json. The blob hash is the primary citation and the prose above is the belt to its braces: if that commit is ever rewritten out from under the reference, the hash still identifies the content and this note still says what it said.

Earlier history, retained: the lazy loader was refined in the generator after this generation was first recorded, so the pinned codegen commit predates it. A second supplemental run was recorded here until 2026-09-18 and was removed then. Its argv was the main argv plus -upstream-version 13.3.29 -- the full binding generation, recorded as a partial one -- and it claimed device.gen.go, unit.gen.go and vgpu_instance.gen.go, which the main recipe reproduces byte for byte from the unpinned header. Its output_selection named a patch and a promote.py inside a scratch directory that no longer exists, so the selection it describes cannot be re-derived. It produced no file this package carries, and a run that owns nothing is not a supplemental run.

nvrtc.note: The package was regenerated to record this entry. It had been carrying a loader older than the generator: binding went straight through purego.RegisterFunc, which panics on a signature it cannot build, making nvrtc the last package that could panic at import. It was also the last package whose Linux candidate list still ended with the unversioned libnvrtc.so, which on a CUDA-12-only host silently bound a CUDA 12 library. Regenerating fixed both; nothing else in the package changed. Regenerated to add the post-load version gate: the loader calls this library's own version entry point once after binding symbols and refuses the load if the major does not match the declared soname major. Re-recorded after repinning cuda_nvrtc from 13.2.51 to 13.4.59 and regenerating: 13.2.51 predates the bundled-headers API, which is what lets NVRTC callers get the CUDA headers on disk for -I instead of hand-declaring fixed-width types in device source.
